reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that inventive learning hinges on the distinction between potential and actual means-end readiness. When an agent encounters a problem, its initial repertoire of actions (means-end-readiness) may not suffice. A roundabout solution emerges when the final act lies outside this initial set. This necessitates a shift from static readiness to dynamic acquisition of new discriminanda and manipulanda. Mathematically, this can be modeled as a conditional probability P(solution | readiness), where readiness evolves through observation and reclassification. The process involves two stages: first, identifying that current readiness is insufficient (S_f ∉ M_e); second, acquiring new capabilities (D_n ∪ M_n) to bridge the gap. The roundabout nature arises because the solution cannot be derived directly from the initial means-end graph but requires expansion into a larger space. This leads to a recursive structure in both GSI (Bayesian updating) and GSE (state-space expansion).
